raw_text: The vineyard has always been under the care of the establishing family. It is one of the last examples of pre-World War II grape growing in the Napa Valley. The methods we still use were once prevalent throughout the valley: no irrigation (not even a drip line to be seen), an organic philosophy (we never jumped on the bandwagon of post-war pesticides), and no trellis systems on our red varietals (these vines are free standing without wire support).

name: Two Acres
raw_text: Cherry, currant, cardamom, tree bark, pine, pepper, rose petal, licorice, cream Very rare to see an old-vine vineyard this high in Mourvèdre, especially in the Russian River Valley. The vineyard used to be approximately 20 acres but was subdivided in the 1970s and sold off for custom home lots. While a few homeowners kept a few vines (more for decoration than anything), only one owner kept a two-acre piece of the vineyard intact. The vineyard was on the brink of death in 1996 but has been carefully restored back to life. “A true gem in Sonoma County! There is little old-vine Mourvèdre in Sonoma County. Yet, here we have two acres of predominantly Mourvèdre planted in 1910. Other varieties planted include Petite Sirah (10%), Syrah (6%), Carignan (4%), Peloursin (3%), and Alicante Bouschet (2%). There are also a few Zinfandel vines in addition to nine whites of a variety called Helena (a white cross of Zinfandel and Mondeuse noir).”

name: Under the Mountain
raw_text: Located at 4590 Redwood Retreat Road Gilroy, CA (west of city of Gilroy in the Santa Cruz Mountains) Several acres of “mixed blacks” (mostly Zinfandel), a couple of acres of Carignane, and one block of Petite Sirah Morgan Twain-Peterson estimates that the vineyard was planted prior to World War One. Surrounded by forest, it is in a beautiful setting below Mt Madonna. Standing among the vines you can see redwood trees above you while experiencing cool afternoon breezes in a very private setting hidden away in the forest.

name: Valsecchi
raw_text: Vineburg, near the town of Sonoma, next to the Vineburg Post Office on Eighth The vineyard – a remnant of a once larger one – was planted around 1900 before being taken over years later by a retired Swiss immigrant dairyman named John Valsecchi (pronounced Valsecky). Today, the vineyard is still in the same family and is looked after by Valsecchi’s grandson and home winemaker Ron Mick. The uniqueness of Valsecchi is enhanced by the fact that it is the oldest vineyard in the Carneros Appellation and one of the cool-climate district’s few Zinfandel vineyards.

raw_text: This 25-acre vineyard lies on a north-facing bench of Sonoma Mountain. POE La Rochelle Alquimista Cellars Lost & Found DeLoach Vineyards Sebastiani Winery bought most of this fruit in the 1950s and earlier, I believe. Ripe red fruits and juicy plum characteristics with a masculine backbone of spicy mountain tannins, lending the grapes an overall earthy forest floor aroma This site has always held cultural and religious significance to the native people of the area. A Pomo creation myth cited Sonoma Mountain as the birthplace of man, much like the Garden of Eden. There are many freshwater springs on this particular bench of the mountain, which we are told brought various neighboring tribes and communities to this site as a neutral trading area. Many native artifacts have been found here and still appear to this day. In more recent history, it has been continuously farmed as a family vineyard for the past 100 years. It has always been a small family business, with the family living onsite and farming many diverse crops and animals in addition to the vineyard and with a continued close spiritual connection to the land. The old vine Pinot Noir is planted on St George rootstock in Spreckels loam soil.

name: Varozza
raw_text: Just north of St. Helena on Pratt Avenue next to the restored winery Expressive black berry, plumb and stone fruits; toasty spice and mineral aromas “The Varozza ranch is an iconic St. Helena landmark featuring an old wood and stone winery that dates back to the days when stonemasons and craftsmen built the original winery for Emil Zange in 1885. Joseph Varozza, who was a St. Helena blacksmith, purchased the property in 1913 and made wine there until his death in 1946. This beautiful property has remained in the Varozza family for the past 97 years! For decades Harold Varozza operated the ranch after his father passed, selling the grapes to local wineries and in 1999 Harold’s son Jack and Jack’s wife Dianna took over the ranch and now produce estate grown wines under their own label: www.varozzavineyards.com … There is a patch of classic head-trained Zinfandel vines that, heading south, connects to a younger block of trellised vines. Planted on stony, alluvial soils between York Creek and the Napa River, the old and younger vines here produce wines that are a little darker with more black fruit than typical of St. Helena with great textural feel and firm structure.” This vineyard contains old-vine blocks of Cabernet Sauvignon, Petite Sirah, and Zinfandel.

name: Vineyard 101
raw_text: Located in Sonoma, this certified organic vineyard was planted in the 1920s. At only 2 ½ acres, it is the smallest site Turley makes into a vineyard designate. The wines are aromatic and light, with lots of fruit and great acidity.

name: Wegat Vineyard
wineries: Bogle, Michael David, Macchia, Soquel Vineyards, Drava, Maley Bros., Lodi Native
raw_text: Bogle, Michael David, Macchia, Soquel Vineyards, Drava, Maley Bros., Lodi Native Ravenswood (1999-2009), Kendall-Jackson, Woodbridge Vineyard Association Joe and Lou Maley planted St. George rootstock on the west side of Lodi and then did their own grafting with Zinfandel budwood in 1958. The vines are head-trained, planted to a 9′ x 9′ vine spacing, and growing in Tokay sandy loam. The vines have nice, loose bunches and typically yield 3 tons/acre. The current owner, Todd Maley, is a founding member of the Lodi Native Project and has produced 10 vintages of Zinfandel bottled for this project from Wegat Vineyard. Wegat Vineyard has been certified for over 10 years in the LODI RULES Sustainable Winegrowing program.

name: Wheeler Vineyard
raw_text: Wheeler Vineyard is the oldest of the four vineyards managed by Circle S Vineyards. It was purchased by Ron Siletto, former president of Almaden Vineyards, in 1995. Tres Pinos Creek runs along its border to the South. The elevated gravelly alluvial terrace on the south side was planted by Bob Wheeler, who used to produce grapes for Almaden, in 1974 to Cabernet Sauvignon (Inglenook), on AxR1 rootstock. The well drained alluvial fan to the north and below was planted in 1977 to plantings of Chardonnay (Wente) for Ken Volk. In 2007, 1.5 acres of Sangiovese (Brunello Grosso) were added to the terrace.

raw_text: Blackberry, plum, cherry, cedar and mint on the nose, elegant minerality on the palate The Old Patch vines are the oldest vines that Ridge farms. They were planted by A. Boutin, a colleague of Luther Burbank, who named his estate Heart’s Desire. Ridge’s Heritage Zinfandel selection from this block is appropriately named Heart’s Desire. Ridge has made wine from these grapes every year since 1966; the Old Patch and Old Carignane blocks are the heart and soul of our Geyserville bottling.

raw_text: Kunde/Wildwood Vineyards & Winery, Martini & Prati, possibly Sebastiani Although the vines have very low yield, the result is a jammy old vine Zin with a rich, earthy, intense dark fruit and chocolate flavor made more complex by aging in American and European oak for 15 months. The 28-acre Century Vine Zinfandel vineyard, a vestige of Louis Kunde’s 1904 purchase, was planted in 1882 by James Shaw. Louis Kunde won a gold medal for this Zinfandel at the 1915 Panama Pacific International Exposition in San Francisco (as well as another gold for a Burgundy, a silver for Cabernet Sauvignon, a Bronze for Riesling and an honorable mention for Sémillon). Louis also shipped grapes to Chicago. According to family lore, Louis once dumped his grapes along the train tracks instead of accepting an insultingly low price upon delivery. Vines were tested by UC Davis in the late 1970s/early 1980s but they were unable to identify the rootstock. The vineyard is head pruned without trellis and dry-farmed.

name: Wirz Vineyard
wineries: Bedrock Wine Co., Stirm Wine Company
raw_text: Farmed by Pat Wirz, this old-vine, dry-farmed vineyard was planted in the 1960s.  It’s located at about 1000′ in the Gabilan Mountains about twenty miles north of the Pinnacles National Monument in the Cienega Valley AVA (San Benito County). Although it lies only twenty five miles east of the cold waters of the Monterey Bay, the coastal influence is dampened by the mountain topography and geology surrounding this site. The San Andreas fault runs through the property highlighting the convergence of two giant tectonic plates.  Granite and limestone are the dominant geologic influence here.  As these rocks eroded over the eons, they weathered into very deep sandy loam (Salinian granite) and clay loam (limestone) with plenty of fist-sized granite and limestone cobbles remaining. The rocky, nutrient poor soil forces the roots to grow deep in search of water and minerals.  These old vines ripen late and are extremely low-yielding at around 1 ton/acre annually.

One of the last of what once was a vast number of old vine primarily Zinfandel vineyards in this neighborhood. Interestingly, it was planted during the early years of Prohibition when grape prices rose dramatically due to the loophole in the national Prohibition law which allowed heads of households to legally produce up to 200 gallons of wine per year tax-free.

We have wine from here dating back to 1978.

name: Alfred Frediani Vineyard
raw_text: Al Frediani’s father bought this land, now prized for quality soils and climate, just after the beginning of the 20th-century, and Al lived there until his passing in 2018 at the age of 96. The Carignane vines existed when Al’s father purchased the land and Al estimated that they were planted in 1901. Al planted the Petite Sirah blocks himself in the 1930s. The soils here at the end of Pickett Road in Calistoga are some of the most beautiful, rocky golden alluvial soils of volcanic origin in all of Napa Valley. The famous vineyard directly adjacent to the southwest has proven the quality of these soils to the public, but insiders and intelligent winemakers have been crowing about the quality of Al’s site for decades. Since 2009, the Petite Sirah and Carignane vine have made up a significant portion of Ritual and beginning in 2010 we have made a vineyard-designate Petite Sirah from these venerable old vines. The vineyard has always been farmed organically and is also dry-farmed. Since Al’s death, his son Steve has taken the reins and continues doing the good work taking care of this treasured vineyard. Updated as of December 2024: Alfred Frediani Vineyard was purchased by Eisele Vineyard in 2023, and the vines have been removed or replanted.

name: Soucie Vineyard
raw_text: Earthy, “forest floor,” dominate notes of black fruits, pomegranate, blackberries, Morello cherries, cassis, plums, strawberries. Planted in 1916 by Kevin Soucie’s grandfather, these vines in the original six-acre block are own-rooted and head-trained in the soil profile classified as DeVries Sandy Loam. The vineyard is 15 miles from the upper reaches of the San Francisco Bay and associated waters. The famous Delta Breeze comes here first and fast, creating diurnal temperature swings of 40-50 degrees almost daily.

name: Viola’s Vineyard
raw_text: 16055 East Hwy 88 Lockeford, Ca 95237 Hwy 88, 2 miles east of downtown Lockeford Planted on a beautiful bluff overlooking walnut orchards and the Mokelumne River. The Zinfandel was planted in 1949-50 with a neighboring cherry orchard to replace Flame Tokays. In 1935, Grandpa Wiederrich and his partners were contract farmers who produced wine from this acreage as part of a winery guild known as the Mokelumne Winery (see sanjoaquinhistory.org ). JRW purchased the property for $10 in November 1943 and continued to grow grapes on it until his death in 1974. Family members have continuously owned it through the present day.
